chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Lodging is due upon the people of the tax (non-Muslims) for three days.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْخَرَاجِ: People of the tax (non-Muslims subject to jizya)

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum duration for forced lodging of non-Muslims according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies that the obligation of lodging (qasr) for non-Muslims (ahl al-kharaj) is limited to three days, a ruling derived from the practice of Imam al-Sadiq (AS). This limitation reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of preventing undue hardship (gharar) on the dhimmi community while ensuring the needs of Muslim travelers or officials are met. The brevity of the period underscores the balance between administrative necessity and justice in Islamic governance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al halby, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The lodging upon the people of the taxation is for three days (no more)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
He (the tax collector agent) stays to demand al-Kharaj from the people of al-Kharaj for three days.’”
